title: Shantideva's Way of the Bodhisattva — the Sanskrit text
author: shantideva
attributionNote: Śāntideva, monk of Nālandā, is named in the tradition as the author of the verses and of the Śikṣāsamuccaya; the work was commented on by Prajñākaramati, whose Pañjikā GRETIL publishes separately, and it is one of the few Indian Buddhist poems still recited daily in Tibetan monasteries. GRETIL's e-text was input by the Digital Sanskrit Buddhist Canon Input Project.
description: The Bodhicaryāvatāra is the manual of the Bodhisattva's course in ten chapters: the praise of the awakened mind and the confession of faults, the keeping of awareness, the guarding of the mind and of the doors of the senses, the perfection of patience, the making of effort, the perfection of meditation and the exchange of self and other, the perfection of wisdom with its analysis of the two truths and of the emptiness of all things, and finally the dedication of the merit of the poem to all beings. It is the most widely loved of all Buddhist philosophical poems, recited as prayer as much as read as argument.
historicalContext: Written at Nālandā and carried to Tibet within a few centuries, where it became the central text of the Bodhisattva training, the work was translated into Tibetan by Sarvajñādeva and Dharmākaraśrī with the help of its Sanskrit commentaries; its Sanskrit text survived in the Nepalese manuscripts and was published in the nineteenth century. The library holds L. D. Barnett's English rendering of 1909 as The Path of Light.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the ten chapters and their 913 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. The file prints the chapter number and the opening homage above each chapter's verses, and the reader drops them. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation.
